words.miss: Look again. Tooth 1 comes to a point, like a triangle.
Look at the tip. Is it flat, or does it come to a point?

teeth.okWhy: Pointy teeth with sharp edges grab and cut meat.
teeth.missWhy: Look at the shape. Sharp, pointy edges are made for cutting meat, not for grinding plants.
teeth.bts: This tooth came from megalodon, a giant shark. Megalodon is extinct. Teeth like this one are found in Florida rivers.

words.miss: Look again. Tooth 2 is wide, not thin.
Look at the top. Are there sharp edges, or round bumps?

teeth.okWhy: Wide, bumpy teeth crush and grind leaves and twigs.
teeth.missWhy: Look at the bumps on top. Bumps crush and grind. Which food needs grinding?
teeth.bts: This is a back tooth from a mastodon, an animal like an elephant. Mastodons are extinct. Their bones have been found in Florida springs.

dig.name: Layer 1 · top
dig.alt: A fossil shell with ribs in pale rock
dig.ask: Look at the fossil from Layer 1. What was this place like when it lived?
dig.clue: A shell with ribs, called a brachiopod. Animals with shells like this live in the sea today.
dig.ok: Yes! A sea animal means this place was under the sea.

miss.1: Look at the clue: shells like this live in the sea, not in sand dunes.
miss.2: Ferns don't have shells. Read the clue again.

dig.envAlt: A shallow sea with coral and sea fans
dig.envCap: Long ago here: a sea · Photo: a shallow sea today, Florida Keys

dig.name: Layer 2
dig.alt: Small footprints pressed into tan sandstone
dig.ask: Now Layer 2. What was this place like?
dig.clue: Tiny footprints in sandstone. Sandstone is made of grains of sand pressed together. Animals walked across these sand hills.
dig.ok: Yes! Footprints across sand hills mean this place was a desert of sand dunes.

miss.0: Footprints are made by walking on dry ground. Read the clue again.
miss.2: There are no plants here, just sand and footprints. Read the clue again.

dig.envCap: Long ago here: a desert of sand dunes · Photo: sand dunes today, Colorado

dig.name: Layer 3
dig.alt: A fern leaf print in red rock
dig.ask: Now Layer 3. What was this place like?
dig.clue: A fern leaf pressed into red mud rock. Ferns grow on warm, wet land near streams.
dig.ok: Yes! Ferns mean warm, wet land with streams.

miss.0: Ferns don't grow in the sea. Read the clue again.
miss.1: Ferns need water, so this was not a dry desert. Read the clue again.

dig.envAlt: A green forest floor covered in ferns
dig.envCap: Long ago here: warm, wet land with ferns · Photo: ferns today, Virginia

dig.name: Layer 4 · bottom
dig.alt: A small fossil trilobite on gray-green rock with a museum label
dig.ask: Last one: Layer 4, at the very bottom. What was this place like?
dig.clue: A trilobite. Trilobite fossils are always found with other sea animals.
dig.ok: Yes! The sea was here too, a very, very long time ago.

miss.1: Trilobites lived with other sea animals, not in dry sand. Read the clue again.
miss.2: Trilobites lived with other sea animals, not on land. Read the clue again.

dig.envAlt: A shallow sea with coral and sea fans
dig.envCap: Long ago here: a shallow sea · Photo: a shallow sea today, Florida Keys

det.alt: A small fossil fish in an oval of pale rock

clues.miss: Look again. Do you see leaf lines, or a body with a tail?
Look again. Are those toe prints, or fins?

det.orgMiss: Look at your clue: fins and a tail. Which living thing has those?
det.envMiss: Fish swim and breathe in water. Try again.
det.bts: This small fish is called Knightia. It lived in a lake in what is now Wyoming, about 50 million years ago.
det.envAlt: A calm lake with trees on the shore
det.envCap: A lake today, like the old lake in Wyoming
det.reveal: This fossil is evidence that a lake once covered this place.

det.alt: A fossil leaf with pointed edges pressed into gray rock

clues.miss: Look again. Leaves don't have fins. What lines do you see?
Look again. These thin lines aren't bones. They branch out like a leaf's.

det.orgMiss: Look at your clue: veins and a stem. Which living thing has those?
det.envMiss: Trees grow with their roots in the ground. Try again.
det.bts: A leaf from a maple-type tree. It fell into an old lake in Utah about 50 million years ago. The tree grew on land nearby.
det.envAlt: A forest floor covered in ferns
det.envCap: A forest today, like the land near the old lake
det.reveal: This fossil is evidence that trees once grew on land here.

det.alt: A gray fossil with many thin ridges in rows

clues.miss: Look again. There is no tail here. What pattern do you see?
Look again. There is no stem. What pattern repeats over and over?

det.orgMiss: Rows of tiny ridges are a clue for coral. Try again.
det.envMiss: Corals only grow in sea water. Try again.
det.bts: Fossil coral from Florida. Corals grow in warm, shallow sea water, so this part of Florida was once under a warm sea.
det.envAlt: A shallow sea with coral and sea fans
det.envCap: A shallow sea today, Florida Keys
det.reveal: This fossil is evidence that warm, shallow sea water once covered this place.

det.alt: Three fossil scallop shells shaped like fans

clues.miss: Look again. These are shells, not bones. What shape are they?
Look again. Is that a stem, or the bottom of a shell?

det.orgMiss: A fan shape with ribs is a clue for a kind of shell. Try again.
det.envMiss: Scallops live in the sea. Try again.
det.bts: Fossil scallops from Virginia, about 4 million years old. Scallops live in the sea.
det.envAlt: A shallow sea with coral and sea fans
det.envCap: A shallow sea today, Florida Keys
det.reveal: This fossil is evidence that the sea once covered this place.

det.alt: Large dinosaur bones sticking out of a rock wall

clues.miss: Look again. These are thick and heavy. Are they leaves or bones?
Look again. What long, thick shapes do you see?

det.orgMiss: Bones this big came from a giant animal. Try again.
det.envMiss: These giants walked on four strong legs. Try again.
det.bts: Dinosaur bones in a rock wall at Dinosaur National Monument, Utah, about 150 million years old. These giants walked on land. A river buried their bones in sand.
det.envAlt: A green forest floor with ferns
det.envCap: Land with plants today, like the land the dinosaurs walked
det.reveal: These fossils are evidence that giant animals once walked on land here.

ask.q: Which tooth looks better for crushing?
ask.ok: Yes. Specimen B is wide with round bumps, good for crushing.
ask.miss: Look at the tops. Which one is wide with bumps for crushing?

ask.q: Which tooth looks better for slicing?
ask.ok: Yes. Specimen A is pointy with sharp edges, good for slicing.
ask.miss: Look at the edges. Which one is pointy and sharp?

result.Bleaf: The wide, bumpy tooth crushed the leaf flat. Crushing breaks up tough plants.
result.Aleaf: The sharp tooth poked holes and tore the leaf, but it didn't grind it up.
result.Aclay: The sharp edge sliced right through the clay strip.
result.Bclay: The bumpy tooth squashed the clay, but it didn't cut it.

curator.A: Sharp slicing edges → likely a meat eater. Specimen A is a tooth from megalodon, a giant shark. Megalodon is extinct. Teeth like this are found in Florida rivers.
curator.B: Wide grinding top → likely a plant eater. Specimen B is a back tooth from a mastodon, an animal like an elephant. Mastodons are extinct. Their bones have been found in Florida springs.
